keyword: how fast does the artemis rocket go
claims: The Artemis Space Launch System (SLS) rocket travels at speeds over 17,000 mph to achieve Earth orbit.
17,000 mph is roughly 22 times the speed of sound.
The upper stage accelerates the Orion capsule to roughly 22,600 mph to transition toward the Moon.
Orion capsule reentry speeds returning to Earth reach approximately 25,000 mph.
The crawler-transporter carries the rocket at a maximum speed of 0.82 mph.
The SLS rocket accelerates the stack to over 17,000 mph to reach low Earth orbit for Artemis II.
The upper stage boosts speed to roughly 22,600 mph to depart for the Moon for Artemis II.
The Orion spacecraft hits speeds of over 25,000 mph when returning to Earth for Artemis II.
The Orion spacecraft reentry speed for Artemis II is faster than previous human spaceflight records.
The 17,500 mph orbital speed is necessary to maintain a stable orbit around Earth before heading to the Moon.
